# Independent D24 retrieval corpus

**Purpose:** Explain the frozen synthetic multilingual relevance oracle and its limits.

`retrieval.json` contains20 independently written source passages and40 manually paired semantic queries, with English, Vietnamese and cross-language groups. Source topics deliberately include related distractors: backups versus restores, OCR versus VLM, chunks versus tokenizer windows, formulas versus cached results, deletion versus retry, runtime health versus actual acceptance. Each query has an explicit relevant source ID; labels are not generated by embeddings or edited after scores are observed. Document/query text is synthetic, not user data or secrets.

Thresholds and selection tolerance are stored alongside the oracle and were fixed before measuring either pinned official model. Metrics use deterministic source-ID tie breaking, true relevant ranks, fraction of relevant sources in top3, reciprocal rank truncated at10 and per-group Recall@3. This corpus is independent of D23's parser reconstruction goldens. It does not measure model generation, OCR transcription, tenant authorization or general multilingual retrieval accuracy.

The measured selected base candidate still misses top3 for `delete-en`, `ocr-vi`, `embedding-vi`; the report retains exact ranks. The small candidate fails quality gates; those failures must stay visible rather than changing labels/thresholds. Source/query text belongs only in this trusted corpus, while tracked benchmark evidence retains IDs, numeric metrics, versions/hashes and rank/top3 arrays without text/vectors. Future broader evaluations require a new corpus version and should keep this baseline reproducible.
